requirement:
The `{term}` role followed by a backtick-delimited full definition name MUST reference a named definition. In rendered Markdown, the reference MUST display the definition's phrase as an ordinary hyperlink to its anchored declaration, without a badge. The phrase MUST be escaped appropriately for rendering.

Missing targets and targets of another kind MUST be reported. Escaped references and references in Markdown code examples MUST remain literal. A term reference MUST NOT satisfy a requirement citation or a Rust function's requirement-coverage obligation.
rationale: **Verdict:** the sources satisfy `requirements.definitions.references`. The implementation is marked completely and the tests cover each obligation. I judged the escaping and code-literal handling by reading the code and the `reference_roles` tests; I did not run anything. **Implementation** - **Role recognition.** `reference_roles` (src/lib.rs) recognises `{term}` followed by a backtick-delimited name and keeps it only if `valid_name` accepts it. It skips matches that are backslash-escaped (`is_escaped`) or inside Markdown code or HTML (`protected_ranges` / `is_protected`). It also protects the `:phrase:` option line of a term declaration. This covers "Escaped references and references in Markdown code examples MUST remain literal". - **Rendering.** `replace_references` (src/lib.rs) turns a `{term}` reference to a real term into a plain `phrase`. - It builds no badge and no shields image. - The href is built by `chapter_href` with the anchor from `DefinitionKind::anchor`. - That anchor matches the `` that `replace_definitions` emits for term declarations. - `terms::escaped_phrase` entity-escapes Markdown-special characters (`* _ ` [ ] \ ~ { }`) and HTML-escapes the rest, which satisfies "escaped appropriately". - A reference with a missing target, or a target of another kind, stays literal in the book. - **Reporting.** `validate_references` (src/evidence.rs) reports a `{term}` reference whose target is missing or not a term ("term X has no matching named definition"). It also reports `{impl}`, `{cite}` and `{test}` references that point at a term or at nothing ("has no matching requirement or example"). - **Terms never count as citations.** Term references `continue` out of the coverage grouping in `validate_references`. `missing_function_references` (src/rust_coverage.rs) excludes `ReferenceKind::Term` and treats `DefinitionKind::Term` targets as not counting. The authoring `references` tool also filters out term references, so they are not offered as citation sites. - **Marking.** The functions that implement parts of this requirement carry `{impl}` markers: `validate_references`, `reference_roles`, `replace_references`, `replace_definitions`, `preprocess_book`, `DefinitionKind::anchor`, `ReferenceKind::label` and `color`, `missing_function_references`, `referenced_terms` and `escaped_phrase`. The escape and protection helpers (`is_escaped`, `protected_ranges`, `is_protected`) carry `{impl}` markers for `requirements.references.markdown_literals` and `requirements.references.targets`. They are therefore covered by sibling requirements rather than left unmarked. I found no unspecified behaviour in the marked code. **Tests** (tests/definitions.rs) - `phrases_are_plain_links_and_markdown_literals_are_preserved` renders a term whose phrase is `*alpha* & `. - It asserts exactly one href `../glossary.html#habeas-definition-glossary.a`. - It asserts no `shields.io` badge. - It asserts the escaped phrase `*alpha* & <beta>`. - Its inline-code, fenced-code and backslash-escaped references stay unlinked, because only one link is produced. - `invalid_declarations_and_reference_targets_are_reported` asserts both errors: "term rules.ready has no matching named definition" (a requirement used as a term target) and "term missing.name has no matching named definition" (a missing target). - `outline_inputs_capture_terms_without_counting_them_as_citations` shows a Rust function whose only reference is `{term}` still gets "no requirement or example citation". This covers the final obligation. - `definition_schema_deletion_and_literal_references_are_checked` asserts that deleting a term gives "no matching named definition". It also asserts that a term reference in inline code, a fenced block, or after a backslash produces no validation errors. **Minor gaps, not enough to fail:** `{impl}`, `{cite}` and `{test}` references to a term are not tested in these particular tests. That behaviour belongs to `requirements.references.targets`.
